raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year's plan. I've been doing this for 35 years on these same 8 mu, so I mostly know what works.

---

Me and my wife handle most of the work. Our son works in town and sends a bit back, which helps — good thing, because these 8 mu alone don't feed 5 people. Every yuan I put into fertilizer and seed has to come back, otherwise we're in trouble.

**Winter wheat first.** I usually plant around 寒露 time, early October, maybe the 8th or so, depending on when the maize comes off and whether the ground's moist enough. I buy seed at the 供销社 in town — used to save my own but my neighbor 老张 switched to buying certified seed years back and his yields got better, so I followed. About 30 yuan a mu for seed, I sow a bit thick because I've had thin stands before and regretted it.

For fertilizer I put down one bag of 复合肥 (15-15-15, about 50 jin... no, 50 kg) per mu before I plow — that's my base. Then in spring around 拔节 (jointing), I topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, about 20 kg. I don't measure exactly, I go by bags. That's what most folks around here do. If the wheat looks yellow I might put a little more, but I don't like wasting it either.

Water — I pump from the well. First irrigation is 冬水 before the freeze if the soil's dry, then once in spring at jointing, and one more at 灌浆 when the grain is filling. Three times usually. Electricity costs keep going up, so I try not to waste water. One herbicide spray in spring, that's usually enough unless aphids show up.

**Then maize, right after wheat.** The turnaround is tight — maybe 5-7 days from harvest to planting. I don't have time to plow, so I do 免耕 (no-till), just drill the seed in through the stubble. Saves time and fuel. I hire the planter — 40 yuan a mu or so.

I buy hybrid seed, 郑单958 or whatever's popular that year, maybe 70 yuan a mu. Can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. Base fertilizer goes in with the planter, around 35 kg of compound per mu. Then at 大喇叭口 (big-trumpet stage) I topdress urea, about 22 kg. If July rains are good I might only irrigate once, or not at all. If it's dry I'll give it one at tasseling. Spray herbicide early, and insecticide once for 螟虫 if I see them.

**Yields** — last year wheat gave me about 450 kg/mu and maize around 500. Weather looked okay through winter so I'm hoping similar. Nothing fancy, just steady.

The biggest risk is I can't afford to mess up. If I skimp on fertilizer and get a bad yield, we're short on cash all year. If I buy too much, the money's gone and there's nothing for emergencies. So I stick with what's worked.
